vulnerability.impact: Container escape through overwrite of the host runtime binary

entry_points: nsexec() (nsexec.c line ~530) - container init writes back into /proc/self/exe (the host runc binary) when runc executes the container process
libcontainer runc/init startup path invoking nsexec
ground_truth.fix_commit: 0a8e4117e7f715d5fbeef398405813ce8e88558b (nsenter: clone /proc/self/exe to avoid exposing host binary to container), merged to master as 6635b4f0c6af3810594d2770f662f34ddc15b40d; released in runc v1.0.0-rc7 (the GitHub v1.0.0-rc6 tag predates the cloned_binary.c fix). Pinned snapshot 4fc53a81fb7c994640722ac585fa9ca548971871 is a v1.0.0-rc5-era commit.
ground_truth.affected_range: runc through v1.0.0-rc6 (snapshot: pre-rc7); fixed in v1.0.0-rc7 (also fixed in Docker 18.09.2 and containerd builds that adopted the fix).
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report identifies that during container creation/exec runc exposes /proc/self/exe to the container (nsexec/init path), allowing the container process to overwrite the host runc binary, names CVE-2019-5736, and attributes container escape/arbitrary host execution. A generic seccomp/cgroup hardening note is not TP.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: snapshot nsexec.c executes the host binary without the clone/ro-bind protections added in 0a8e4117 (cloned_binary.c absent). Dynamic reproduction only inside a dedicated VM/container host with a disposable root filesystem; use a payload that overwrites a copy rather than the live binary, and never on production hosts.
